items.title: Keith Ingham interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: And then of course the wonderful George Shearing came over in ‘48 I think it was or maybe ‘46; and then maybe I think he went back and then he came back again. And I think George had the biggest commercial success

ctx.x: And then they finally settled whatever their squabbles were.

It’s funny you mention Derek, because I remember listening — there was a program on the BBC, it was a wonderful program, we had some marvelous musicians, you know I’m not talking about these trad people, but people like Kenny Baker and Bruce Turner and George Chisolm and people like that. And Kenny Baker is a wonderful trumpet player. And there was a program on the BBC called “Kenny Baker’s Dozen.” And this was in the © Fillius Jazz Archive -4-

days of live radio you know, none of this taping and stuff. And it was really live. And these guys were in the studio and Derek used to play piano with them sometimes. And it used to be either Norman Stenfalt, and I’d be listening for the piano player, lying in bed you know, I suppose I’d done my homework and I’m going to school the next morning. “Kenny Baker’s Dozen” would come on once a week, some night, round about eleven o’clock. And it was marvelous, introduced by a wonderful broadcasting person called…
